description: Adversarial import fixtures for the import pipeline's matcher (T1.3). Each case is independent: import its files, in import_order, into an empty ledger. 'transactions' is the ground truth: the distinct transactions the ledger must end with. Every row of every file names the transaction it is ('transaction'), so rows sharing a key are one transaction and rows with different keys are distinct, whatever the import order. 'outcome' is the pipeline outcome expected when importing in import_order.

cases.title: Daily $2.90 fares across a January/February statement overlap
cases.what_it_tests: Same merchant, same amount, adjacent days. Fares posted a day or two after the ride share posted dates with the neighbouring day's fare, so a date-set overlap rule merges distinct rides. Rows posted on 2026-02-01 appear in both downloads and ARE the same transactions.

cases.title: Generic NAME text with the merchant only in MEMO, re-downloaded with new FITIDs
cases.what_it_tests: A credit union sends NAME 'POS PURCHASE' or 'ACH DEBIT' and puts the merchant in MEMO. Different merchants share amount and day; a second download of the month regenerates every FITID. True duplicates must be found by MEMO, and same-day same-amount rows at different merchants must stay distinct, including a third one that only appears in the second download.

cases.title: A bank that recycles short FITIDs
cases.what_it_tests: FITIDs are short sequence numbers the bank reuses. The same FITID on a different date and amount is a different transaction; the same FITID on the same date with a different amount and merchant is too. A row repeated in the overlap with the same FITID and the same facts is a duplicate.

cases.title: A CSV reference number shared by different transactions
cases.what_it_tests: Bank of America card CSV. A refund carries its purchase's reference number, and a later purchase reuses an earlier reference. Same reference does not mean same transaction; the re-download's repeats are duplicates.

cases.title: Two cards that both end in 4821, at different banks
cases.what_it_tests: Imported with automatic account matching. Each card's QFX carries its own full account number; the Capital One CSV only prints the last four. They are two accounts and must never be merged, and the CSV belongs to the Capital One card (same institution, same last four).

cases.title: One OFX file with two statements for the same account
cases.what_it_tests: The bank answers a two-month request with one statement per month in one file. Both belong to the same account. The statements overlap on 2026-04-30 and repeat that row with the same FITID: one transaction, even though both copies are in the same file. Two $20.00 ATM withdrawals on 2026-05-02 are two transactions.

cases.title: A pending dinner, its tipped settlement, and a same-price takeout three days later
cases.what_it_tests: A $40.00 dinner shows as pending on 2026-03-06 and settles at $48.00 with the tip. On 2026-03-09 the same restaurant charges exactly $40.00 for takeout. The pending item settles into the $48.00 row (same purchase date), not into the exact-amount takeout; the takeout is a new transaction. An earlier $40.00 lunch on 2026-03-03 appears in both downloads.

cases.title: A Barclays CSV (purchase dates only) and the QFX of the same month
cases.what_it_tests: The CSV gives only the purchase date; the QFX gives the posted date and DTUSER. Each CSV row is the same transaction as its QFX twin. Two $36.50 ramen dinners two days apart (one posts on the other's purchase date) must pair by purchase date, not cross over.

cases.title: A Barclays CSV (purchase dates only) against a QFX with posted dates only
cases.what_it_tests: A constructed variant: the QFX has DTPOSTED but no DTUSER, two days after each purchase. The CSV rows (purchase dates) are still the same transactions as the QFX rows. No two rows share amount and merchant, so the pairing is unambiguous.

cases.title: The same Chase card as a posted-only QFX for February and a CSV with purchase and posted dates from 02-27
cases.what_it_tests: Chase's QFX gives posted dates only; its CSV gives purchase and posted dates. A daily $2.90 fare crosses the boundary. The windows overlap on posted 02-27 and 02-28: the two 02-26 rides posted then are in both files (true duplicates). The 02-27 and 02-28 rides both post 03-01 and are only in the CSV, so their purchase dates fall on QFX rows' posted dates: they are different rides. Imported in both orders.

cases.title: The same Chase card as a posted-only QFX for February and a CSV with purchase and posted dates from 02-27 (reverse order)
cases.what_it_tests: Chase's QFX gives posted dates only; its CSV gives purchase and posted dates. A daily $2.90 fare crosses the boundary. The windows overlap on posted 02-27 and 02-28: the two 02-26 rides posted then are in both files (true duplicates). The 02-27 and 02-28 rides both post 03-01 and are only in the CSV, so their purchase dates fall on QFX rows' posted dates: they are different rides. Imported in both orders.

cases.title: An Amex CSV with purchase dates only against the Amex QFX with posted dates only
cases.what_it_tests: A $4.75 coffee every day, posting two days later. The QFX ends at posted 04-15 and the CSV starts at purchase 04-14, so no coffee is in both files: every coffee is a different purchase even though rows a day apart sit within three days of each other. The only true twin is a $23.88 Amazon order bought 04-14 and posted 04-15, the one row within three days with no lookalike. Imported in both orders.

The only true twin is a $23.88 Amazon order bought 04-14 and posted 04-15, the one row within three days with no lookalike. Imported in both orders.

cases.title: A pending row and its posted version in the same download
cases.what_it_tests: A Citi export made while a dinner was settling lists it twice: pending at $40.00 and cleared at $48.00 with the tip. They are one transaction, though both rows are in one file. An Uber ride still pending stays pending.

cases.title: Two checks with the same amount, day and description
cases.what_it_tests: Wells Fargo shows checks as 'CHECK' with the number in its own field. Checks 1043 and 1044, both $150.00, clear on 05-12: two transactions. The CSV re-download repeats both (matched by check number, not by text) and adds check 1045, also $150.00 on 05-12.

cases.title: A $20 ATM withdrawal and a $20 Zelle payment sharing FITID 77
cases.what_it_tests: Chase checking reuses the short FITID 77: on a $20.00 ATM withdrawal on 03-02 and on a $20.00 Zelle payment on 03-04. The month download holds both, with the same FITID in one file. Two transactions; the ATM row in both downloads is one.

cases.title: OFX 'POS PURCHASE' with the merchant in MEMO against a CSV with the full description
cases.what_it_tests: PNC's QFX puts 'POS PURCHASE' in NAME and the merchant in MEMO; its CSV writes 'POS PURCHASE <merchant>' with no memo. Shell (QFX) and Chevron (CSV), both $40.00 on 03-10, are different purchases. H-E-B $61.20 on 03-12 is in both: the same purchase (CSV text = NAME + MEMO).
